subject: Clarify EU packaging/pricing & per-vector vs per-token for embeddings
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@stratum.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@stratum.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:03 -0400
Subject: Question on embeddings packaging for EU pilot

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising for our similarity search. Before we push to a pilot with our EU tenant, our procurement team asked for a clearer breakdown of how you price embeddings. A couple of specific questions: 

- Do you bill embeddings as per-vector units or per-token for the hosted API? We have mixed tooling and I want to confirm how our usage will be counted.
- How are dimensions accounted for? If we move from 1536 to 3072 dims for higher recall, is that double the unit price or handled differently?
- Which models are currently supported for embeddings under the hosted plan (open models + Redwood-verified)? Any limitations for EU regions?
- We also need to understand the EU tax/VAT treatment on monthly invoices and whether Redwood can provide an invoice without VAT (we are VAT-registered) or will you charge VAT by default for the EU region?

We have an internal MRPC (minimal required procurement checklist) — I attached a short PDF with the legal/invoicing fields we need. Could you point us to the right ratecard SKU and, ideally, a short example invoice for a baseline pilot (30M vectors/day, mixed dims)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — the pilot kickoff is scheduled for the first week of June.

Best,
Alex
StratumAI — Head of Platform

Attachments: Stratum_MRPC_request.pdf (application/pdf)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@stratum.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:05:40 -0400
Subject: Re: Question on embeddings packaging for EU pilot

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list and the MRPC — that's helpful. Quick answers up front, then Ben will follow with technical/volume guidance: 

- Billing model: hosted embeddings are billed as per-vector units. We report units in vectors; we do not currently meter embeddings by token. There is a mapping guide in the ratecard for older token-based flows.
- Dimensions: price scales by vector-dimension tier. For example, 1536-dim sits in the baseline tier; 3072-dim is in the "high-dimension" tier and carries a higher per-vector rate (not strictly double). We provide a dimension multiplier table in the spreadsheet attached.
- Supported models (hosted, EU region): atlas-emb-small, atlas-emb-large, redwood-emb-2, and several community-curated open models we ship with verified perf. The ratecard entry flags models with EU hosting availability.
- VAT/Tax: Redwood invoices EU customers based on the billing address and VAT registration status. If you provide a valid VAT ID, we can zero-rate VAT on the invoice where applicable; otherwise standard VAT will be applied. We can generate a draft invoice for the pilot to show line-item VAT treatment.

I've attached the public embeddings ratecard (spreadsheet) and a one-page example invoice for a 30M-vector pilot. Ben — can you confirm the expected vector/day sizing and give guidance on cost ranges if Stratum mixes 1536 and 3072 dims across requests?

Next steps: once you confirm the mix (percentage per-dimension) we'll run a short cost estimate and provide a formal pilot quote. Happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

—Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: redwood-embed-ratecard-2027-05.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), example-pilot-invoice.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@stratum.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:34:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Question on embeddings packaging for EU pilot

Alex — quick technical note from infra/SE perspective: 

- Per-vector billing: yes — each embedding request returns N vectors (one per input item). We count vectors after any client-side batching/expansion, so be mindful of pre- vs post-processing.
- Dimension pricing: we use dimension bands. Roughly: up to 1024 dims = baseline unit; 1025-2048 = +30% per-vector; 2049-4096 = +65% per-vector. This is to reflect memory and throughput costs across our serving runtime. Exact multipliers are in the attached spreadsheet that Lauren shared.
- Model compatibility: redwood-emb-2 is the recommended default for most use-cases (good perf/cost). atlas-emb-large has higher-quality vectors for semantic search but costs more per-vector. EU-hosted model availability is controlled by the region flag in the ratecard; there are no model-quality differences other than architecture/size.
- Mixed-dimension example: for your pilot if 70% of vectors are 1536 and 30% are 3072, we would compute a weighted average unit price using the dimension multipliers and then multiply by projected vector count.

I ran a quick back-of-envelope: 30M vectors/day * 30 days = 900M vectors/month. If your mix is 70/30 (1536/3072) and baseline rate is $0.0000025 per 1536-vector (illustrative), effective monthly cost is ~ $2,430 before any volume discounts or reserved-commit pricing. We can do a formal workbook if you want line-by-line.

Two operational notes: enable prefix caching for frequently repeated IDs (reduces billed vectors because of caching at request layer) and consider short-lived dense re-embeddings for incremental updates instead of re-embedding whole documents — can change cost materially.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
